title: Skybase's discretionary subsidy spending runs through a multisig where the external GovOps provider holds the majority of signers
content:
Beyond the primitives, A.6.1.1.4.3.4 records that "Skybase uses capital to provide Subsidies to incentivize strategic markets to promote USDS demand." The funding path is explicit: "the source of capital ... is the Skybase Treasury. Skybase Treasury capital is transferred to the USDS Demand Subsidies Multisig for utilization" (A.6.1.1.4.3.4.1).

The control structure is the substance. The multisig "is controlled by two (2) signers from Operational GovOps Soter Labs and one (1) signer from Skybase Foundation" (A.6.1.1.4.3.4.2) with a 2-of-3 threshold (…2.2). Usage is bounded to "disburse funds on behalf of Skybase to fund strategic USDS demand incentive opportunities" (…2.4).

Do the arithmetic on who can move money. Soter Labs alone holds two signatures and meets the threshold; the Skybase Foundation holds one and cannot act at all without Soter Labs. The Agent's own affiliate is a minority that can neither spend nor veto. Discretionary subsidy capital is effectively administered by the external GovOps provider, with the Foundation as a participant rather than a controller.

That is a deliberate inversion of the usual arrangement, where a service provider co-signs and the principal controls. It matches the pattern seen in the rebate distribution (A.6.1.1.4.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3), where Operational GovOps — not Skybase — holds execution. Across both, the Atlas systematically separates *deciding to spend* from *being able to spend*.

The residual exposure is concentration rather than self-dealing: this is unpriced discretionary spending, outside the primitives and their tracking methodologies, controlled by a single external firm meeting quorum on its own.
description: Treasury capital moves to a 2-of-3 USDS Demand Subsidies Multisig with two Soter Labs signers and one Skybase Foundation signer, so the Agent's own side cannot disburse alone.
